posts.body:
Congratulations and Good Luck!!!!

I had my 2 girls 8 weeks ago (also by c-section) at 35+5 weeks.

here is the website for MOMS. http://www.moms-hongkong.com/

I haven't yet joined, but I plan to very soon (I have the application form sitting on my table ready to post!).

I know a few mums who have had twins over the last couple of months - seems to be a growing trend!

Enjoy the relative rest as much as possible while you can....get lots of massages too!!

K

posts.body:
Hi L, We did a LOT of research on the stroller topic till I was dizzy with the details. This one definately is the Mercedes Benz of them all and will last for years so a good investment. Drawback= weight (15kgs) but I found that you will always have to compromise on something. We were lucky it came up on the Asia Xpat website for sale and is in pristine condition. Cost us 3000 HK$. Most of the simple ones cost $2500 anyway. A new one is expensive around double that, but still a good investment. Besides I love its snazzy design. 

Hows the pregnancy going? I am huge at 35 weeks, can hardly sleep and oscillate between fear and joy (these are our first babies). Do you know the sex of your babies? 

Cheers

Elizabeth

posts.body:
hi elizabeth

It's hard work - but I'm sure you realise that! It's like plunging into the deep end...you just have to get on with it! and YOU WILL COPE!!

I also have a 2 year old, so not first time parents, which means not quite so scarey, but we have the added trauma of a toddler running about the place.

I BF for the first 4 weeks, then got mastitis and it was very painful. I now give them both Expressed BreastMilk + formula via bottle (which actually works really well for us because it means others can feed one or both if I'm caught up with my son). When I was breastfeeding I preferred to do them seperately because you still have to burp / change nappies seperately....but on occasion I did them at the same time (ie, when they were both screaming down the house).

They are both girls (non identical).

K
